ai.description: *Leptobrachella lateralis* is a small toad (25–28 mm) with a brown dorsum, dark lateral stripes, and white-spotted flanks. It features a distinctively granular skin texture and dark-barred limbs.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Leptobrachella lateralis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, broad, dark brown lateral band that extends from the snout through the eye to the groin.
ai.habitat: *Leptobrachella lateralis* inhabits primary evergreen forests in the mountains of Nagaland, typically found near clear, rocky streams at elevations between 1,500–2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Nagaland Asian Toad is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates along the damp, mossy banks of fast-flowing mountain streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Leptobrachella lateralis* breeds in streams during the monsoon, laying small clutches of large, unpigmented eggs attached to the undersides of submerged rocks.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Leptobrachella lateralis* is endemic to the high-altitude forests of Nagaland in Northeast India, typically occurring at elevations between 1,500 and 2,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The call of *Leptobrachella lateralis* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, metallic chirps emitted from rocky, fast-flowing mountain streams.
